Billionaire Ron Lauder, president of the World Jewish Congress and once one of Benjamin Netanyahu’s closest associates, has broken years of silence to speak out against the Israeli prime minister in an interview with Haaretz. 
Lauder says he saw 30 years ago how Netanyahu put his own political future ahead of the country’s, and is now determined to wake up the Israeli public before it is too late. 
He has cut his ties with Israel over the past year, telling Haaretz “I sold my house in Tel Aviv” and saying he gave his Beersheba property to the Jewish National Fund, which he chairs. 
Addressing Israelis, he said: 
“Your fathers fought for the country, and you’re losing everything because of stupidity.”

NEW: U.S. Forces Japan will ban all BYD vehicles from Kadena Air Base in Okinawa, citing security risks. 
The ban applies with no exceptions to personnel’s private cars, contractor vehicles, taxis and delivery vans, with security forces turning them away at every gate. 
Kadena, the largest U.S. Air Force base overseas, hosts the 18th Wing and the Typhon missile system capable of launching Tomahawk cruise missiles. 
Base spokesperson Lt. Col. Alli Stormer said the vehicles “present an unacceptable and unmitigable risk to our personnel and our mission,” without giving details. 
Yonhap, citing U.S. military officials, said the concern is that cameras, sensors, GPS and connected features could collect and leak sensitive information.

Flames were spotted on the rear fuselage of a Ukrainian Antonov An-124 Ruslan cargo plane during or just after landing at Chubu Centrair International Airport near Nagoya, Japan. 
The aircraft, operated by Antonov Airlines, was arriving from Fairbanks, Alaska, at around 19:20 local time when air traffic controllers noticed the fire. 
Airport fire crews responded, and the plane briefly stopped on the runway before taxiing to its parking spot under its own power. 
The cause is under investigation, with some Japanese reports pointing to a possible problem with the auxiliary power unit, while the extent of any damage and the cargo remain unknown. 
Antonov Airlines, which has operated out of Leipzig, Germany, since Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine, has not yet commented in detail.

NEW: Warhound, a Texas defense-tech startup backed by Anduril founder Palmer Luckey and Colossal Biosciences CEO Ben Lamm, has emerged from stealth with a plan to clone and gene-edit military working dogs. 
The company raised a $200 million seed round at a $1.2 billion valuation from investors including Sequoia Capital, ARK Invest and In-Q-Tel, the CIA-backed venture arm. 
It aims to reduce U.S. reliance on Europe, which supplies more than 80% of American military working dogs, fewer than half of which complete training due to health and performance problems. 
Warhound will clone top-performing Belgian Malinois, German Shepherds and Labradors through Colossal-owned Viagen, and edit out genes linked to career-ending conditions such as hip dysplasia and some cancers, with possible future enhancements like wolf-derived scent genes. 
Anduril will supply armor and sensor-equipped vests, with its role described as “on top of the dog, not in the dog.” 
Led by former Pentagon chief data officer David Spirk, the company expects its first puppies in early 2027 and aims to have dogs in service by around 2029.
